## Colours in flowers and fruits

Why is a tomato red and a marigold orange? In flower petals and fruits, plastids hold pigments other than chlorophyll: yellow, orange or red. These plastids are **chromoplasts**, from the Greek word *chroma*, meaning colour. Their bright colours attract pollinators and the fruit-eating animals that help in seed dispersal.

<!-- STEP -->
## Plastids with no colour

Some plastids have no pigment. These colourless plastids are **leucoplasts**, from the Greek word *leukos*, meaning white. They store food such as starch, oils or proteins. In potato and taro (Colocasia) cells, they store starch. A white petal, such as jasmine, also has colourless plastids.
